sentences.text: Leaellynasaura was a small, slender herbivore belonging to the ornithischian group of dinosaurs.
This animal moved on two legs with a light build, featuring a beak, four-toed feet, and long limbs.
While recent estimates suggest a body length of roughly 180 centimeters, the total length including the tail could reach up to 3 meters.
Its tail was exceptionally long, measuring three times the length of the rest of its body and containing more vertebrae than any other ornithischian except certain hadrosaurs.
This creature lived and thrived in polar Australia, a region further south than any modern reptile could survive.
Fossil evidence from a skull fragment reveals enlarged eyes and large optic lobes, indicating an adaptation for seeing in low light.
The species was first found in the Eumeralla Formation at Dinosaur Cove, Australia, where four recorded fossil occurrences have been identified.
Tom Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich named the genus in 1989 in honor of their daughter, Leaellyn Rich.
As a herbivore, its diet consisted of low-growing vegetation such as horsetails, cycads, and ferns.
The unworn crowns of its upper teeth possessed up to five cusps on the inner and outer edges.
Research by Herne in 2009 argued that this dinosaur lacked ossified tendons in its tail, a feature absent in more advanced ornithischians.
Scientists debate whether the large eyes were an adaptation for darkness or simply a trait of a juvenile individual.
Contemporaries likely endured polar conditions where the sun might not rise for several weeks or months during winter.
A 2019 study recovered the animal as a member of the clade Elasmaria, and it belongs to the parent group Elasmaria.
Recent studies have not reached a consensus on its classification, with some analyses describing it as a non-iguanodontian ornithopod and others as a basal neornithischian.
In a 2013 revision, Herne could not confidently assign long-tailed postcranial skeletons to the species, leaving only the holotype cranium and a few specific elements.
Leaellynasaura lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, specifically from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
During this time, the province of Victoria, Australia, was located within the Antarctic Circle.
